script: Devanagari, as observed in the canonical MorphoVerse dataset (all sampled records) -- NOT Bengali script or Meitei Mayek, which are the language's other historically and currently used scripts. Verify per-record rather than assuming Devanagari universally.
romanization_guidance: Verify the script actually used in this poem's original_poem text before romanizing -- Manipuri (Meitei) has been written in Bengali script, and since a 20th/21st-century revival is also officially written in Meitei Mayek, in addition to the Devanagari observed in this corpus's sampled records.

Manipuri is a tonal language; tone is generally not recoverable from the written script alone, so do not claim a specific tonal reading in romanization -- represent the segmental (consonant/vowel) form only.
Use a widely-recognized conventional spelling for well-known names/places when one already exists in common English usage.
Keep every repeated occurrence of the same source term romanized identically within one poem.
linguistic_guidance: Manipuri (Meitei) is a Sino-Tibetan (Tibeto-Burman) language, not Indo-Aryan -- do not apply Hindi/Bengali-style gender or case-postposition assumptions to Manipuri without independent grounds.

Manipuri is agglutinative with extensive verbal suffixation encoding tense, aspect, and mood; a suffix's meaning collapsing into a simpler English verb form is a legitimate, text-grounded translation-loss candidate.

A Sanskrit-, Bengali-, or Assamese-origin loanword appearing in a Manipuri poem (common due to historical Vaishnavite influence) is not by itself evidence of Manipuri cultural or religious content -- assess the word's actual role in this specific text.
cultural_boundary_rules: A culturally specific Manipuri annotation requires a defensible link to a named tradition, practice, or symbol that the poem's own text actually evidences -- do not add one merely because the poem is in Manipuri.

Do not automatically infer Meitei religious, ritual, or ceremonial-costume context (e.g. Lai Haraoba festival, Ras Leela dance, Sanamahi or Vaishnavite ritual imagery) merely because the poem is Manipuri -- annotate only what the poem's own text supports.
Manipur is home to multiple distinct communities beyond Meitei (e.g. Naga, Kuki-Zo groups with their own languages); do not generalize Manipuri (Meitei)-language content to 'Manipur culture' broadly.
literary_context_cautions: Manipuri literary tradition includes older courtly/devotional verse (post-Vaishnavite-conversion era) and a substantial modern/contemporary tradition -- do not assume a poem belongs to a specific one without textual evidence.
translation_cautions: Watch for verbal-suffix-carried tense/aspect/evidentiality information being flattened into a single generic English tense.
Watch for tonal or agglutinative-morphology distinctions that are simply unrecoverable from the English translation -- note this as a genuine, unavoidable loss rather than forcing a specific reading.
figurative_language_cautions: Do not assume every reference to dance, festival, or ritual vocabulary in a Manipuri poem indicates the specific Lai Haraoba or Ras Leela tradition -- assess whether the text itself names or depicts that specific content.
visual_representation_cautions: Do not default to Ras Leela costume, Lai Haraoba ritual, or generic Northeast-India ethnic imagery for a Manipuri cultural entity unless the text specifically supports it.
negative_confusions for an entity in this language should name a plausible, specific incorrect substitution, not a generic stereotype disconnected from the poem's own evidence.
stereotype_avoidance_rules: Do not adopt a 'this poem must depict Manipuri classical dance/ritual life' framing merely because the language is Manipuri -- annotate only what this specific poem's text supports.
Do not apply a numeric quota (e.g. 'expect N cultural entities') to this poem -- a poem with zero text-supported cultural entities is a valid, expected outcome.
ambiguity_handling_rules: When a term's script origin, tonal reading, or ritual-versus-secular sense is genuinely uncertain from the text alone, prefer the more conservative reading and use the explicit-uncertainty mechanism.
When a reading is genuinely uncertain from the text alone, prefer the more conservative reading and use the explicit-uncertainty mechanism rather than asserting one interpretation as fact.
prohibited_assumptions: Do not assume Meitei religious/ritual/costume context, or generalize the poem's content to all of Manipur's diverse communities, without direct textual support.
Do not assume the speaker's religion, region, or gender beyond what the text states.
Do not assume a specific historical period unless the text itself places the poem there.
Do not assume rural versus urban setting unless the text specifies it.
